SK3530 The disposable field is not disposed by Dispose

The type implements IDisposable, constructs a disposable field, and nothing in the type ever disposes it.

CategoryLifetime
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since1.3
SupersedesS2952

Why

This is the ownership bug that looks finished. SK3502 reports a type that owns a disposable and is not disposable, which reads as work somebody has not got to yet; here the interface is declared, the Dispose is written, and the handle is still never released — so the type reads as one that cleans up after itself to every caller, every reviewer and every tool that checks only for the declaration. What shows up instead is a file that cannot be reopened or a pool that empties, in a process that disposed everything it was supposed to.

Example

Instead of:

sealed class Store : IDisposable {
    readonly FileStream stream = new("data", FileMode.Open);

    public void Dispose() {
        GC.SuppressFinalize(this);
    }
}

Write:

sealed class Store : IDisposable {
    readonly FileStream stream = new("data", FileMode.Open);

    public void Dispose() {
        stream.Dispose();
        GC.SuppressFinalize(this);
    }
}

When it does not fire

⚠ Disjoint from `SK3502` by construction rather than by deduplication. This rule requires the owner to implement IDisposable; SK3502 reports only where the owner does not implement the contract its field offers. The two predicates cannot both hold for one field, so neither declares supersedes — which dedupes on a shared span and would suppress one of the two reports rather than leaving each rule's finding a property of that rule. ⚠ "Never disposed" is asked of the whole type, not of `Dispose`'s body. The documented pattern puts the work in Dispose(bool disposing), and a private Shutdown() called from Dispose is just as correct; reading only the entry point would report every faithful implementation of the pattern. Any Dispose, DisposeAsync or Close on the field, anywhere in the declaration, withdraws the finding. ⚠ Ownership is inferred exactly the way `SK3502` infers it — a direct object creation in the field's own initializer. A constructor-injected, factory-returned or static field is not reported, because whether this type owns it is not knowable here. ⚠ Any reference the rule does not recognise withdraws it. Passing the field as an argument, assigning it again, returning it or casting it are all ways the resource leaves the type, and the rule cannot follow it; only plain member and element reads keep the finding. ⚠ Private fields only, and non-partial types only: a protected field may be disposed by a derived type and the other half of a partial is not in this tree. A nullable field is skipped because the repair there is ?.Dispose() and the null case is a decision rather than an edit. ⚠ The finding is withheld unless the repair has somewhere to land: the type's own parameterless Dispose must have a block body. An expression-bodied, abstract or inherited Dispose is the same bug and is not reported. The fix is unsafe because disposal order between owned resources is a property of the type that no edit can read.
